content: The interplay between mineral extraction volumes and the requisite supply chain infrastructure forms the foundational basis for assessing current and future transport demand. An analysis of the projected commodity transport demand based on mining expansions in South Africa between 2020 and 2024 reveals a distinct and robust growth trajectory. During this period, transport demand demonstrated an overall increasing trend, beginning at a minimum value of 145.2 million tonnes in 2020. This upward momentum was sustained over the subsequent years, ultimately reaching a maximum volume of 185.0 million tonnes by the end of 2024. This significant expansion in tonnage underscores the escalating pressure on South Africa’s logistics networks and highlights the critical need for scalable transport solutions capable of accommodating surging bulk freight requirements. For example, the introduction of the MINESHIFT 2026 platform in early 2026 represents a strategic industry effort aimed at advancing Africa's mining beneficiation capabilities [31] . Such platforms signal a transition toward more sophisticated processing within the continent, which will inevitably alter the spatial distribution of transport demand and require logistics providers to adapt to new nodes of industrial activity [31] . Furthermore, direct capital investments into mining infrastructure provide concrete signals of impending volume increases. A prominent illustration of this is the long-term commitment demonstrated by Gold Fields, which outlined a planned R1.714 billion investment into the South Deep Expansion Project spanning the 2026 to 2027 period [33] . Instead, strategic investments must be made in fleet optimization, advanced routing algorithms, and collaborative partnerships with mining entities. As rail network rehabilitations remain a prolonged work in progress, the bulk logistics industry in South Africa has become increasingly strategic. The combination of rising mining output and the expansion of regional trade corridors is driving a pronounced need for sophisticated, road-based infrastructure and agile transport solutions, a dynamic explicitly noted in industry trend analyses from May 2026.
